hints: Multiplying by 100 makes a number bigger. Count the zeros in 100.
Move the decimal point to the right, one place for each zero.
Start at 3.45 and move the point two places to the right.

solution.methodName: Multiply or divide by 10, 100, 1000: move the point

steps.action: 100 has two zeros, so move the decimal point two places.
Multiplying makes the number bigger, so move the point to the right.
steps.why: Each move to the right makes the number 10 times bigger. Two moves make it 100 times bigger.

steps.action: Move it one place: 3.45 → 34.5. Move it again: 34.5 → 345.

trapNotes.34.5: This moves the point only one place. That is × 10. For × 100, move it two places.
trapNotes.0.0345: This moves the point to the left. That is ÷ 100. Multiplying makes the number bigger.
trapNotes.3,450: This moves the point three places. That is × 1000. 100 has only two zeros.
